reason: The named characters in this passage are Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and Joshua (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ). Each occupies a position of religious or military authority and leadership. Moses is the prophet-lawgiver and divine intermediary; Aaron is the priest performing ritual functions; Joshua is Moses' military aide. None of these individuals are portrayed as regular, ordinary people—all are presented in exceptional roles with special responsibilities and direct involvement in sacred matters. While the passage frequently references 'the people' (הָעָם) collectively, these references are anonymous masses, not named individual characters.
